clue.text: Game of chance? Pay odds outside

indicators.note: the odd letters of the word pay sit outside, wrapping the other piece
odds means the odd-numbered letters of the next word, first and third

parts.note: luck is chance, fortune

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to pay the odds on a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game of chance' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' alone is the definition. 'odds' takes P and Y from 'Pay', and 'outside' wraps them around LUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means brave and willing, a synonym of spirited and courageous.

clue.text: A fall inside, but worker is bearing up well

indicators.note: a worker that is bearing something carries it within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a prole is a proletarian, a working-class worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for well is read bottom to top

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Someone survives a fall but suffers internal injury, though the worker is coping well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing up well' looks like a phrase about coping, but splits into the container signal 'is bearing', the reversal signal 'up' (APS), and the piece well.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolapse is the medical slipping down of an organ inside the body, literally an internal falling.

clue.text: Removing tie and uniform, navy psychiatrist catches cold

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the psychiatrist catches the cold, holding the letter within his name

parts.note: R. D. Laing was a famous Scottish psychiatrist
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A naval psychiatrist strips off tie and uniform and comes down with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts C inside LAING. R. D. Laing was a well-known Scottish psychiatrist of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlacing a shoe or corset means undoing its ties, so it is removing a tie.

clue.text: Praise for solving unfinished sudoku

indicators.note: solving a puzzle works its letters out afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged
unfinished means the last letter of the puzzle name is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone earns praise for working out a sudoku they had left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final U to leave SUDOK, and 'solving' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is acclaim or prestige earned by an achievement, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Yielding nothing crooked to cross pass

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: the crooked word goes across the other, straddling it on both sides

parts.note: bent means crooked, either curved or dishonest
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Someone corrupt gives way, refusing to cross a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a noun, a gap in mountains, but is the verb meaning to pass away; 'to cross' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding means submissive and compliant, which is what an obedient person is.

clue.text: A display of balance by Kent batsmen at crease

indicators.note: to crease something is to crumple it, so these words are crumpled into a new order

explanation.surface: Kent's batsmen at the crease put on a display of balanced, steady batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crease' looks like the cricket batting line, but it is the anagram signal: crumple the letters of KENT BATSMEN AT. Kent is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank statement is a document showing an account's balance, a witty reading of a display of balance.

clue.text: Flying moves provide a little excitement

parts.note: a drop is a small amount of liquid, a little
kicks means thrills or excitement, as in doing it for kicks

explanation.surface: Daring manoeuvres in the air add a small thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, a flying kick off the half-volley is the drop kick, so the definition is fair. 'provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop kicks are rugby kicks made as the dropped ball bounces, and also airborne kicks in wrestling.

clue.text: Bringing up medicine to a couple raised in the city

indicators.note: in means the reversed word is placed inside the postcode letters

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an item is a romantic couple

explanation.surface: A doctor brings medicine to a couple who grew up in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reads the couple word upwards, as this is a down clue, and 'in' is the container signal. The City of London, its financial district, has the postcode prefix used here.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a drug given to cause vomiting, so it is medicine for bringing up stomach contents.

clue.text: Punk rock tried to embrace nihilism, initially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters embrace, holding the first letter within them
to rock something is to shake it, so the letters are shaken into a new order
initially means take only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Punk rock bands attempted to adopt nihilism as their creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punk rock' reads as a music genre, but 'Punk' is the definition and 'rock' the anagram signal on TRIED. 'to embrace' puts N, from 'initially', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk is an old word for rotten wood used as touchwood, and tinder is dry material for starting fire.

clue.text: Call for attention with a display, when drunk

parts.note: oi is a shout to catch someone's attention
an LED is a light-emitting diode, used as a display

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for attention and shows off when they have been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for being intoxicated, as in well-oiled.

clue.text: First group playing an instrument

parts.note: a band is a musical group
first is number one
on means performing or playing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: The opening band is playing an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'band one on', the first group playing. A bandoneon is a South American button accordion used in tango.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandoneon is a kind of concertina, a musical instrument found in tango orchestras.

clue.text: Superb old rose hybrid shows sign of life

indicators.note: a hybrid rose is bred by mixing, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A splendid old hybrid rose is still showing signs of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' looks like part of the gardening description, but it signals that the letters of SUPERB OLD ROSE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood pressure is a vital sign measured to show that the circulation, and so life, continues.

clue.text: They came before playing 10 across

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them around into a new order

parts.note: 10 is written out as the word ten

explanation.surface: Earlier generations used to play the accordion-type instrument in 10 across.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 across' seems to point at another answer, but the words TEN ACROSS are rearranged. 'playing' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are people who lived before you in your family line, the predecessors who came before.

clue.text: Return note with grass blade

indicators.note: return means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: E is a musical note
a fink is an informer, as is a grass in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a musical note along with a blade of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns E + FINK backwards. 'grass' looks like a lawn but is British slang for an informer, as is fink.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a cutting tool consisting of a sharp blade.

clue.text: A musical drama?

definitions.meaning: a show with singing and dancing in it
a fuss or commotion, making a great fuss

explanation.definitionFit: Song and dance is both a stage entertainment and an idiom for a needless fuss or commotion.

clue.text: They may be told to dance off with opponents

indicators.note: off means the letters are disordered, gone wrong

parts.note: in bridge, East and South sit as opponents, E and S

explanation.surface: Some people are told to go and dance off with their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told to' reads as an order, but 'to' is part of the anagram with DANCE and ES, and 'off' signals it. East and South are on opposing sides at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Short amusing stories are things one tells, so the definition describes them by what is done with them.

clue.text: Deposit crew in rising waters?

indicators.note: in means the crew word is placed inside the other
in a down clue, rising means read upwards

parts.note: tides are moving waters of the sea
the crew of a ship are its men

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is put ashore as the waters rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' gives SEDIT, read upwards, and 'in' is the container signal. The question mark admits that waters for tides is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit.

clue.text: Plant key behind reptile house

indicators.note: behind places the key after the other pieces

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Del is the delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone hides a plant behind the reptile house at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key but is the Del key on a computer keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a plant of the lily family, the flower of Greek myth.

clue.text: Peer wearing band on cape for valour

indicators.note: on means the first part sits before the cape in this across clue
the band is worn by the peer, wrapped around him

parts.note: a fess is a horizontal band across a heraldic shield
an earl is a peer of the realm
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A nobleman wearing a sash over his cape is decorated for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: A fess is a horizontal band in heraldry; 'wearing' is the container signal and 'on' puts that part ahead of the cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearlessness is the quality of having no fear, which is courage or valour.

clue.text: Waste energy breaking mugs

indicators.note: the energy letter breaks into the other word, splitting it

parts.note: mug is slang for a face
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone wastes energy smashing mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts E inside FACES. 'mugs' looks like cups but is slang for faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Faeces is bodily waste matter, excrement.

clue.text: Bill given apple turnover

indicators.note: a turnover turns the word over, so it is read backwards, upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a rennet is a variety of dessert apple

explanation.surface: A diner is charged for an apple pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apple turnover' reads as a pastry, but 'turnover' reverses RENNET, an old apple variety. A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound or ten-dollar banknote, a bill.

clue.text: Change at noon?

definitions.meaning: noon is the point when the morning, the a.m., ends

explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or revise, and read as a.m. end it is the moment noon arrives.

clue.text: Mean drunk provides watery food

indicators.note: a drunk slurs words, so the word for mean comes out sounding different

parts.note: mean, ungenerous, is selfish

explanation.surface: A stingy drunkard supplies seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for mean, said with a drunken slur, turns its S into SH. 'Mean drunk' looks like a nasty drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfish are water creatures with shells, such as crabs and oysters, eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Free bricks — around a tonne

indicators.note: the bricks go around the tonne, enclosing it

parts.note: Lego is a brand of toy building bricks
T is the abbreviation for a tonne

explanation.surface: Some bricks weighing about a tonne are given away for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'approximately', but it puts LEGO around T.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to release it, to set it free.

clue.text: Make fleeces with short back and tailored front

parts.note: to fleece is to swindle, to con

indicators.note: back means the word for short is read in reverse

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt

indicators.note: front means the first letter of the word tailored

explanation.surface: A barber gives sheep's fleeces a short back and sides with a neat front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short back and' recalls the haircut, but 'back' reverses CURT into TRUC and 'front' takes T from 'tailored'.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct is to build or assemble, to make something.

clue.text: Pulled a King from the river

indicators.note: from means these letters are taken away from the word for pulled

parts.note: tweaked means pulled sharply, as of a nose
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: Someone dragged a monarch out of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Tweed runs along the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the border between England and Scotland.

clue.text: Gave emphasis to pushing leaves back across square

indicators.note: the word for leaves goes across the square letter, straddling it
back means the whole combination is read in reverse

parts.note: to desert is to leave, abandon

explanation.surface: Someone pushing the leaves back over a square makes a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts S inside DESERTS to give DESSERTS, and 'back' reverses the lot. 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a word or point is to give it emphasis.

clue.text: Ladies at Glastonbury, say, give up rings at gate

indicators.note: to give up something is to let it go, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a Portaloo is a portable toilet hired for outdoor events like Glastonbury
O is ring-shaped, so two rings are two Os

explanation.surface: Festival toilets at Glastonbury hand back the rings at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a big English music festival, and a Portaloo is the British brand name for its portable toilets. 'give up' removes the two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a doorway or entrance, so a gate.
